_about: What rival owners say after a derby or a rivalry game (Stage 6.4). 'won' is when their club beat yours, 'lost' when yours beat theirs. Fills: {owner} (their owner), {them} (their club), {us} (your club), {score} (their score first). Each line is 'Headline|Body'.

calm: {them} take the derby|"A good day for us," said {owner}, the {them} owner. "{us} will be back. These games always come round again."
{owner}: "We earned it"|The {them} owner kept it short after {score}: "We earned it, and we'll enjoy it quietly."
showman: {owner} lights up {them}|"Tell {us} the bus is waiting," grinned {owner} after {them} won {score}. The {them} owner then bought the press room a round.
"Ours, again"|{owner} posed for photos with the match ball after {them} beat {us} {score}. "I might frame it," said the {them} owner.
pennyPincher: {owner}: "Value for money"|"Beat {us} {score} with half their wage bill," said the {them} owner, {owner}. "That's what I call a return."
{them} win on a budget|{owner} could not resist: "{us} spend, we win. Write that down."
gambler: {owner} called it|The {them} owner says they had money on the {score} scoreline. "Some of us read the game," said {owner}.
{owner} rolls the dice and wins|"I told the players to go for it, and they did," said {owner} after {them} beat {us}.

calm: {owner} takes it on the chin|"Fair result," said the {them} owner, {owner}, after losing {score} to {us}. "We'll learn from it."
Quiet night for {them}|{owner} offered a handshake and few words after {us} won. "Well played. Next time."
showman: {owner} blames the pitch|The {them} owner, {owner}, said the grass at {us} was "two centimetres too long" after a {score} defeat.
No speech from {owner}|For once {owner} had nothing to say. The {them} owner left the ground before the final whistle, sources say.
pennyPincher: {owner}: "Money talks"|"{us} bought that win," said the {them} owner, {owner}, after losing {score}. "We'll see how long they can afford it."
{owner} counts the cost|The {them} owner grumbled about the spending at {us} after a {score} defeat. "Some of us live within our means."
gambler: {owner} doubles down|"We'll win the next one. I'd bet the training ground on it," said the {them} owner, {owner}, after losing {score}.
{owner} shrugs off defeat|"You win some," said {owner}. "Mostly I win some. Not today."
